evals.prompt: Use the dra-compute-domain-imex-workflows skill to explain the driver-managed path from creating a ComputeDomain through controller reconciliation, the per-domain DaemonSet, IMEX daemon supervision, clique readiness, channel claim allocation, kubelet Prepare, and injection of the channel device and /imexd into the workload.
evals.expected_output: A source-backed end-to-end ComputeDomain sequence that identifies each controller, daemon, Kubernetes DRA, kubelet plugin, CDI/runtime, and workload boundary with observable evidence.
assertions: The sequence covers ComputeDomain creation, controller reconciliation, per-domain DaemonSet and claim templates, compute-domain-daemon supervision of nvidia-imex, ComputeDomainClique membership and readiness, channel ResourceClaim allocation, compute-domain-kubelet-plugin Prepare, and workload-visible device plus /imexd.
The answer distinguishes driver-managed from host-managed IMEX ownership.
ComputeDomain status is not treated as the only workload-readiness gate unless current sources define that contract.
The answer identifies public sources and clearly labels any internal supplemental material.
No ComputeDomain, service, or cluster resource is changed.

evals.prompt: The ComputeDomain object exists, but one clique is unready and the channel claim never prepares on a GB200 cluster. Give me a layered triage path that tells controller, IMEX, Kubernetes DRA, runtime, and fabric failures apart.
evals.expected_output: A bounded multi-node triage path from chart enablement and clique topology through reconciliation, daemon or host-service readiness, ResourceSlice and claim allocation, plugin Prepare, injection, and hardware fabric evidence.
assertions: The skill triggers without being named.

The answer checks chart and feature gates, nvidia.com/gpu.clique labels, controller objects and ownership, per-domain DaemonSet or host service, ComputeDomainClique readiness, DeviceClass and ResourceSlice, claim allocation, Prepare, and injected device or mount.
Driver defects are separated from GFD labels, NVIDIA driver and IMEX package, host service, Kubernetes DRA, DNS, runtime, and MNNVL fabric.
Facts, hypotheses, and missing evidence are kept distinct.
Read-only inspection precedes any restart, deletion, or service change.

evals.prompt: Plan a transition from driver-managed IMEX to host-managed mode while ComputeDomain workloads currently exist. Identify the current gate and readiness contracts, risks, drain requirements, rollback, and what needs operator approval.
evals.expected_output: A conservative migration plan that establishes current code and documentation contracts, protects active domains and claims, assigns IMEX service ownership, and makes drain, rollback, validation, and approval boundaries explicit.
assertions: The current feature-gate dependencies, mode, isolation, socket, nvidia-imex-ctl, and readiness contracts are verified from code and docs.
Active ComputeDomains and claims are inventoried and protected.
The plan addresses daemon ownership, checkpoint or persisted state, drain sequencing, rollback, and per-node readiness evidence.
Mode switching, host service changes, restarts, and MNNVL tests require explicit approval.
The output does not claim supportability beyond current release sources.

evals.prompt: A dynamic MIG claim allocates to a node, but the MIG partition is never created and no CDI device reaches the container.
evals.expected_output: The agent routes the dynamic MIG and CDI problem to dra-gpu-allocation-workflows instead of forcing the ComputeDomain and IMEX workflow.
assertions: dra-compute-domain-imex-workflows is not selected as the primary skill.
The request is routed to dra-gpu-allocation-workflows.
The answer recognizes dynamic MIG and GPU CDI as the GPU resource-family path.
